newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Rubber - S.E.Asian markets subdued ahead of holiday.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - S.E.Asian markets subdued ahead of holiday.

text.p: Southeast Asian rubber markets are expected to be very quiet this week ahead of the Chinese New Year and moslem holiday period, combined with subdued demand from major consumers, regional traders said on Monday.
The coinciding of the Eid al-Fitr and Chinese New Year will see Malaysian markets closed between Thursday, February 6 and Tuesday February 11.
"The rubber market has been quite dead for a long time and I don't see reason for people to do anything before the two festivals," said a Malaysian trader.
She said prices were also expected to soften by "one or two cents" in the current week as pressure mounted on local suppliers to match cheaper rubber prices in the region.
At the close of last week, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted the benchmark February RSS 1 buyer at 298 Malaysian cents a kg. February SMR 20 buyer was at 293.50.
Ample supplies of raw materials, following an improvement in weather conditions, was weighing on prices, said traders.
They said plantations will stop tapping rubber for nearly a week during the two festivals.
Drum latex was offered by trading houses at 233-234 Malaysian cents a kg FOB on Friday.

In Indonesia, traders also expected tyre-grade SIR20 rubber prices to remain weak in the short-term amid slow foreign demand. They said March SIR20 was done at 53.00 U.S. cents a lb fob Padang on Friday afternoon, up by 0.50 cents a lb from morning levels. Offer prices were unchanged in Medan and Surabaya at 53.00 U.S. cents a lb.
"What I can say is that dealers expect the price to improve a bit this week. But we know that demand is still very, very low," said one dealer.
Dealers said poor consumer demand from the United States, China and Europe had dampened market sentiment.
"Prices usually become firmer because of Chinese demand, but now only the markets in Europe, South Korea and Latin America are still active," said one dealer.
Dealers said they expected prices to improve in the coming weeks, but added that offshore customers were still reducing stocks.
In Thailand, rubber prices drifted lower last week, pressured by ample supplies and slow demand, trade sources said.

Traders said they were disappointed that the current low offer prices have drawn only limited buying interest from Japan and China. Buying from the United States is also not expected in any significant volume as the U.S. is believed to be unwinding large rubber stocks.
"Buying from Japan was rather moderate and China is virtually absent from the market. Prices have also been pressured by robust supplies," said one Hat Yai trader.
Thai rubber supplies entering the market last week rose 14.67 percent from the previous week to 58,719 kgs, an auction market souce told Reuters.
Benchmark RSS3 for February shipment was quoted around $1.20 a kg FOB Bangkok on Friday. Some traders quoted as low as $1.18 a kg compared with $1.20-1.22 a kg in the previous week.
STR20 was quoted around $1.18 a kg and latex dropped to $0.90 from $0.91-0.93 a kg on the same basis.
The market expects prices to firm in February when wintering in the south, Thailand's biggest rubber producing area, tightens supplies.
-- Singapore newsroom, +65 870-3174
